settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: The project's XMLParserSettings defines secure defaults (SECURE_PROCESSING=true, DISALLOW_DOCTYPE_DECL=true, external general/parameter entities=false), showing intended hardening, but DocumentUtil does not use them.
No caller of DocumentUtil.getDocument was found via search_text in main source, so runtime reachability is unproven.
Modern JDK default DocumentBuilderFactory implementations may disable some external entity resolution by default, which could reduce or eliminate the impact.
candidates.description: DocumentUtil.getDocument(URL, ...) creates a DocumentBuilderFactory, sets validating/namespaceAware/schema, then calls builder.parse(InputStream) directly. It never calls setFeature(XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, true), never disables external general/parameter entities, and never disables DOCTYPE declarations. If the URL points at attacker-influenced XML, the default JAXP DocumentBuilder can process external entities/DTDs (XXE, SSRF via external DTD URL, and entity-expansion DoS) depending on the JAXP implementation in use. This is a real instance of an XML parser without the hardening that XMLParserSettings/XMLReaderBasedParser apply elsewhere in the project.
missing_evidence: Whether any externally reachable code path calls DocumentUtil.getDocument with untrusted XML.
The actual JAXP implementation and its default feature settings at runtime.
Whether a Schema passed in also constrains entity resolution in practice.
preconditions: A caller passes a URL whose XML content is attacker-influenced (remote or user-controlled).
The active JAXP DocumentBuilder implementation resolves external entities/DTDs by default.
candidates.title: DocumentUtil.getDocument parses XML via DocumentBuilderFactory without XXE/secure-processing hardening

counter_evidence: XMLReaderBasedParser.getXMLReader() and AbstractSPARQLXMLParser both set compulsory secure features on the reader, mitigating for those parsers.

In XMLReaderBasedParser, feature-setting failures are swallowed as warnings (SAXNotRecognizedException/SAXNotSupportedException -> reportWarning), so even there the hardening is best-effort rather than guaranteed.
No main-source caller of SimpleSAXParser() (no-arg XMLReader) was confirmed via search.
candidates.description: createXMLReader() chooses an XMLReader from the 'org.xml.sax.driver' system property, else SAXParserFactory (namespaceAware true), else Xerces. In none of these branches does it set FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, disallow-doctype-decl, or disable external-general/parameter-entities. Any consumer that uses the returned reader directly (e.g. SimpleSAXParser's single-arg constructor, which calls XMLReaderFactory.createXMLReader()) and does not subsequently apply XMLParserSettings features obtains an unhardened reader, allowing XXE/entity-expansion DoS on untrusted XML. Higher-level parsers (XMLReaderBasedParser, AbstractSPARQLXMLParser) do apply the secure features afterwards, so exposure depends on the specific consumer.
missing_evidence: Identification of any attacker-facing code path that parses XML with a reader from XMLReaderFactory.createXMLReader() without later applying the secure features.
Default SAX feature state of the JAXP/Xerces reader actually selected.
preconditions: A consumer uses XMLReaderFactory.createXMLReader() (directly or via SimpleSAXParser) and parses untrusted XML without applying secure settings itself.
candidates.title: XMLReaderFactory.createXMLReader() returns XMLReader without setting secure SAX features

counter_evidence: Defaults are secure for standard Xerces/JAXP readers, which recognize these features, so the warnings would not normally trigger.
AbstractSPARQLXMLParser applies the same settings and additionally sets an ErrorHandler.
Features are attempted on the reader created internally, not on external input.
candidates.description: In XMLReaderBasedParser.getXMLReader(), each compulsory feature (SECURE_PROCESSING, DISALLOW_DOCTYPE_DECL, EXTERNAL_GENERAL_ENTITIES, EXTERNAL_PARAMETER_ENTITIES) is applied inside a try/catch that catches SAXNotRecognizedException and SAXNotSupportedException and only calls reportWarning(...) instead of failing. If the underlying XMLReader does not recognize/support a security feature (or a custom XMLReader without the features is supplied via XMLParserSettings.CUSTOM_XML_READER), parsing continues with the reader's default behavior. This means the nominally compulsory XXE/entity protections may silently not take effect, which is a defense-in-depth concern rather than a definite vulnerability.
missing_evidence: Whether any deployment uses a CUSTOM_XML_READER lacking these features.
Whether reportWarning surfaces to operators or is silently logged.
preconditions: The configured XMLReader does not support one or more of the compulsory security features (e.g. a non-Xerces reader or a custom reader).
Untrusted XML is then parsed by that reader.
candidates.title: Secure SAX feature configuration errors are downgraded to warnings, allowing silent fallback to insecure parser defaults
